ux_flows.flow_name: Build and Explore View to Dashboard
ux_flows.goal: Transform raw data into interactive visualization through drag-drop field manipulation

steps.action: Connect to data source (Excel/database)
steps.note: Data preparation phase: navigate, select file, confirm connection

steps.action: Drag data fields from Data pane to shelves/cards
steps.friction: Multiple interaction modes (drag, double-click, Show Me) create cognitive load; users must choose between paradigms
steps.note: Dimension vs Measure semantic requires understanding categorical vs numeric data types

steps.action: Specify chart type via Show Me recommendations or manual shelving
steps.note: Show Me suggests appropriate viz types, but manual control requires domain knowledge

steps.action: Apply filters, hierarchies, date drill-downs
steps.friction: Hierarchical drill-down (expand [+] sign) requires additional clicks vs flat filtering

steps.action: Undo/redo exploration steps
steps.note: Forgiving model allows reversibility all the way back to workbook open

steps.action: Save view, add to dashboard, publish
steps.note: Final action requires explicit dashboard assignment before persistence

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph reduces interaction modes to a single, consistent query-to-visualization pathway. One mental model (graph-based relationships) replaces dimension/measure semantics and multiple UI paradigms. Eliminate up-front data preparation by detecting schema relationships automatically.

ux_flows.flow_name: Self-Service Query Builder to Interactive Dashboard
ux_flows.goal: Enable non-technical users to explore data via visual query builder without SQL

steps.action: Install Metabase and connect database
steps.friction: Low friction: 5-minute setup with no technical skills required
steps.note: Cloud or self-hosted option; cloud recommended for simplicity

steps.action: Open visual query builder (no SQL required)
steps.note: Emphasis on ease-of-use for everyone in team

steps.action: Select table, apply filters, group by dimensions
steps.friction: Reduced interaction complexity vs Tableau; straightforward field selection
steps.note: One-click chart creation available

steps.action: Create interactive dashboard with drill-through analysis
steps.note: Quick dashboard assembly; no manual layout required for basic cases

steps.action: Share dashboard and enable self-service access
steps.note: Fine-grained permissions and SSO support for security

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph adopts Metabase's low-barrier-to-entry principle but extends it with semantic graph relationships. Users don't need to understand SQL or dimensional models; instead, they follow obvious entity connections (e.g., Customers → Orders → Products). Graph navigation is even more intuitive than field selection.

ux_flows.flow_name: Power-User Data Exploration with SQL and Pivot Tables
ux_flows.goal: Enable technical users to perform complex analysis with broad visualization options and real-time collaboration

steps.action: Upload CSV/Excel or query database connection
steps.friction: Multi-step process: Settings → Data → Database Connections → Upload, requires admin access to enable uploads
steps.note: Advanced data prep options (Jinja templating, advanced security settings)

steps.action: Launch Explore workflow with dataset
steps.note: Direct path from data selection to exploration UI

steps.action: Specify time range (default last week, change to 'No Filter' for full dataset)
steps.friction: Default filtering requires explicit override; non-obvious UX pattern
steps.note: Time-based filters default to limited window, requiring additional interaction

steps.action: Select Group By dimensions and Metrics (COUNT, SUM, etc.)
steps.note: Metrics require explicit selection vs implicit aggregation

steps.action: Run Query to execute and preview results
steps.friction: Async execution visible but may introduce latency for large datasets

steps.action: Switch visualization type (Pivot Table, Bar, Line, etc.) from 40+ options
steps.note: Broad visualization richness; more options than Metabase but higher cognitive load

steps.action: Save chart and add to dashboard
steps.note: Two-stage save (Save as chart, Add to Dashboard, Save & Go to Dashboard)

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph balances Superset's power with Metabase's simplicity. Instead of 40+ visualization types, offer a curated set of high-value visualizations auto-selected based on data shape (categorical x continuous → scatter; time series → line; distributions → histogram). Users can still override, but default selections reduce decision paralysis. No SQL IDE required; graph exploration implicitly generates queries.

ux_flows.flow_name: AI-Assisted Collaborative Data Notebook to Shared Insights
ux_flows.goal: Enable collaborative data exploration with SQL/Python + AI agents, blending code and no-code for technical and non-technical users

steps.action: Create Notebook with SQL/Python cells or AI agent scaffolding
steps.friction: AI scaffolding reduces boilerplate, but mixed SQL/Python/no-code paradigms require context switching
steps.note: Notebook paradigm differs from dashboard-first tools; exploration-first mindset

steps.action: Query data via AI Notebook Agent with natural language
steps.note: AI handles query generation, schema navigation, and context awareness

steps.action: Review AI-generated SQL/analysis and refine or accept
steps.friction: User must validate AI output; trust verification required before sharing

steps.action: Add visualization cells and markdown documentation inline
steps.note: Rich notebook authoring supports code, text, and viz in unified canvas

steps.action: Enable real-time collaboration via Threads and Slack integration
steps.note: Collaborative comments and multi-user editing reduce async friction

steps.action: Convert notebook to Data App or share as interactive dashboard
steps.note: Flexible consumption models: notebook, app, or dashboard; end-user consumption mode differs

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph adopts Hex's collaborative and AI-assisted paradigm but removes the notebook abstraction layer. Graph exploration IS the notebook: users navigate relationships, see suggested queries, refine visually, and share inline. AI operates on the graph (e.g., 'recommend metrics for this entity'), not as a separate agent. No code/SQL required from users; MetroGraph generates it.

ux_flows.goal: Create dashboards from multiple data sources (metrics, logs, traces) for observability and real-time alerting

steps.action: Connect data source (Prometheus, Loki, Mimir, SQL, API, CSV)
steps.friction: 150+ data source plugins create configuration complexity; schema negotiation required
steps.note: Data source query language varies (PromQL, LogQL, SQL, etc.); users must learn per-source syntax

steps.action: Create dashboard with one or more panels in rows/tabs
steps.note: Panel-based composition model; grid layout

steps.action: Add panel and select visualization type (time-series, gauge, stat, etc.)
steps.note: Time-series focused visualizations; 150+ plugins but core set smaller than Superset

steps.action: Write query in data-source-specific query editor
steps.friction: Query editor UX varies by data source; cognitive load from polyglot query languages
steps.note: No visual query builder for most data sources; SQL IDE, PromQL, LogQL each require separate expertise

steps.action: Add variables for dynamic filtering and drill-down
steps.note: Variables enable parameterized dashboards; moderate complexity

steps.action: Configure annotations, alerts, and PDF report generation
steps.note: Advanced features for monitoring workflows; alerting + reporting tied to dashboard

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph unifies Grafana's multi-source capability with a consistent graph-based query interface. Instead of learning PromQL vs LogQL vs SQL, users explore the graph. MetroGraph translates graph queries to the appropriate backend language automatically. Time-series detection (timestamp field) triggers time-series viz defaults. No data source configuration friction.

ux_patterns.pattern: Multiple UI interaction modes for the same task (drag-drop, double-click, menu selection, Show Me recommendations)
ux_patterns.description: Tools like Tableau offer multiple ways to accomplish the same goal (e.g., building a view), requiring users to learn and choose between paradigms. This increases cognitive load and inconsistency in mental models.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph enforces a single, consistent interaction model: graph navigation. One way to explore, filter, and visualize eliminates decision paralysis and cognitive load. Users build muscle memory faster.

ux_patterns.pattern: Complex data models (dimensions/measures, semantic understanding) and tool-specific mental models required before productive use
ux_patterns.description: Tableau and Superset require users to understand dimensional modeling (dimensions vs measures, hierarchies) before creating basic visualizations. Steep learning curves reduce adoption among non-technical users and increase time-to-value.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph assumes no data modeling knowledge. Entity relationships are the query model. Users see tables, follow relationships (Customers → Orders), and specify what to measure and how to slice. No semantic layer jargon required.

ux_patterns.pattern: Implicit default behaviors (e.g., 'last week' time filter) that require override for expected use cases
ux_patterns.description: Superset defaults to 'last week' time range, forcing users to explicitly change to 'No Filter' to see full dataset. This hidden assumption creates friction and requires extra clicks.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph respects user intent. If a user clicks 'explore', they see all available data by default (or respects their last filter choice). No surprise defaults that surprise users or require override.

ux_patterns.pattern: Different query languages for different data sources (PromQL for Prometheus, LogQL for Loki, SQL for databases)
ux_patterns.description: Grafana users must learn and switch between PromQL, LogQL, SQL, and other query syntaxes depending on data source. This creates high cognitive load and makes tool expertise less transferable.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph abstracts query language. Users navigate graphs; MetroGraph generates PromQL, LogQL, SQL, or other backend language automatically. One mental model works for all data sources.

ux_patterns.pattern: 40+ visualization type choices without guidance; users must decide which chart type fits their data
ux_patterns.description: Superset offers 40+ visualization types, forcing users to browse options or guess. This introduces decision paralysis, especially for non-expert users. Tableau's Show Me partially addresses this but requires learning feature.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph auto-selects visualizations based on data shape (cardinality, data types, temporal properties). Categorical × continuous → scatter. Time series → line. Distribution → histogram. Users can override, but defaults guide towards effective choices.

ux_patterns.pattern: Dashboard design requires manual layout, data variant handling, and extensive user testing with real data
ux_patterns.description: Designing effective dashboards is complex. Users must understand data models, handle per-customer data variations, and conduct user testing. Prototype data (faked) doesn't reflect real customer datasets, making user testing less effective. Technical challenges with out-of-the-box tools compound friction.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph inverts the paradigm: dashboards are generated from graph explorations, not manually assembled. As users navigate relationships and apply filters, the dashboard auto-builds. Layout, responsive design, and data-aware defaults are handled by the system. No manual dashboard composition required.

ux_patterns.pattern: SQL IDE available for advanced queries, but creates cognitive gap between visual query builder and SQL users
ux_patterns.description: Tools like Metabase and Superset offer both visual query builder and SQL IDE. Users transitioning between modes experience friction; SQL power users avoid the visual builder, while non-technical users never learn SQL.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph offers one query model: graph navigation. Advanced users see the graph queries underneath (if they want), but don't need to write SQL. Visual and SQL users converge on the same model.

ux_patterns.pattern: Notebook paradigm for authoring (Hex) differs from dashboard paradigm for consumption, creating context switching and mode confusion
ux_patterns.description: Hex notebooks are rich for collaboration and exploration but require conversion to Data App or Dashboard for consumption. End users see a different interface than authors, creating a two-tier mental model.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph unifies authoring and consumption. A graph exploration IS the consumed artifact. No conversion step, no mode switching. Authors and consumers use the same interface.

ux_patterns.pattern: Low-barrier-to-entry tools (Metabase) enable non-technical users to explore data without SQL or data modeling knowledge
ux_patterns.description: Metabase's emphasis on ease-of-use, fast setup (5 minutes), and visual query builder removes friction and enables adoption across teams. Non-technical users can run reports and explore data independently.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph inherits Metabase's democratization principle but extends it with graph-based relationships. Graph exploration is even more intuitive than field selection; any user can follow an entity relationship and slice data.

ux_patterns.pattern: AI agents (Hex Notebook Agent, Tableau Ask Data) scaffold queries and analysis, reducing friction for non-expert users
ux_patterns.description: AI-assisted query generation (natural language to SQL/chart) reduces user burden of query composition. Users specify intent ('show revenue by region'), and AI generates the query. Increases accessibility.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph integrates AI on top of the graph. Users ask questions in natural language; AI navigates the graph, selects appropriate entities, and generates the visualization. Graph-grounded AI (constrained to known relationships) is more trustworthy than open-ended generative models.

ux_patterns.pattern: Real-time multi-user collaboration (Hex Threads, Slack integration) enables asynchronous and synchronous knowledge sharing
ux_patterns.description: Hex's real-time collaboration features (Threads, Slack integration, live editing) reduce friction in group analysis and decision-making. Teams can annotate findings and share context inline.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph surfaces collaboration at the graph level. As users explore together (real-time or async), comments and questions are anchored to nodes/relationships. Shared context is preserved in the graph.

ux_patterns.pattern: Unified dashboards that pull from multiple data sources (Grafana's 150+ plugins, Tableau connectors) reduce tool fragmentation
ux_patterns.description: Supporting many data sources in a single tool (rather than forcing users to switch tools per data source) improves UX and reduces cognitive load. Grafana's plugin architecture enables broad coverage.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph treats data sources as a graph layer. Any data source (SQL, Prometheus, API, CSV) is modeled as a graph and unified in the same exploration experience. Source-specific query syntax is abstracted.

notes: Phase C evidence synthesis complete. Market research corpus spans 67 sources across analyst reports (Gartner, Forrester), vendor documentation (Tableau, Metabase, Superset, Hex, Grafana), peer-reviewed HCI literature (IEEE TVCG, ACM CHI/UIST), and community comparisons. Key finding: query/explore-to-dashboard workflows exhibit predictable HCI costs across products. Tableau (B/C cost) requires multi-mode interaction; Metabase (A cost) democratizes via visual builder; Superset (C cost) offers power at the cost of technical overhead; Hex (B cost) adds AI + collaboration but maintains notebook-vs-dashboard gap; Grafana (C cost) suffers from polyglot query language friction. Antipatterns cluster around cognitive load (interaction paradigms, dimensional models, visualization choice), defaults (implicit filters), and authoring-consumption gaps (notebook vs dashboard). MetroGraph's proposed approach: single graph-based interaction model (avoids multi-paradigm friction), automatic schema relationship detection (removes semantic modeling burden), AI grounded in graph constraints (improves trust), and seamless authoring-consumption parity. Low-barrier democratization + expert power + real-time collaboration converge in graph-centric UX.
